subject: chemistry
title: Properties and Particle Pictures
welcome_lead: Why can you squash a gas but not a brick? Particle pictures hold the answer.
meta_desc: Compare properties of solids, liquids and gases through particle arrangements in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now explain real-world behaviour using particle diagrams.

concepts.def: How much mass is packed into a given volume.
Squashing a substance into a smaller volume.
Ability to move and change shape; liquids and gases flow.
Tiny back-and-forth motion of particles in a solid.
The unpredictable movement of gas particles.
Particles in gases have more kinetic energy than in solids.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most solids are denser than liquids because the particles are packed closer. Gases are usually the least dense because their particles are spread far apart.
Solids and liquids cannot be compressed much because their particles are already touching. Gases can be compressed a lot because there is plenty of empty space between particles.

Liquids and gases both flow because their particles can move past each other. Solids do not flow because particles are locked in place.

More movement means more flow.

mcqs.q: Why can gases be compressed easily?
options: There is empty space between gas particles
